bihar_raw_news.content: Home > Bengal > Bengal launches ‘Seva First’ innovation challenge Bengal Bengal launches ‘Seva First’ innovation challenge BY Dipali Sen 21 Sept 2026 1:31 AM IST X Dipali Sen 21 Sept 2026 1:31 AM IST Kolkata: The West Bengal government on Saturday launched the ‘Seva First Innovation Challenge – Eastern Zone’, inviting students, researchers, start-ups and innovators from West Bengal, Bihar and Jharkhand to identify real challenges in their surroundings and develop practical solutions. The online portal, sficeast.wb.gov.in, was launched at the IIT Kharagpur Research Park in New Town as part of the ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan 2026’. The Department of Science & Technology and Biotechnology (DSTBT) is the nodal department and is organising the initiative in association with six other state departments. The challenge has two categories. School, ITI and polytechnic students and undergraduates can participate in the Junior Category, while graduates, young professionals, researchers, early-stage start-ups, independent innovators and community groups can participate in the Open Category. Participants will be encouraged to identify problems in villages, towns, schools, workplaces and communities, understand whom they affect, develop solutions and demonstrate their impact through implementation. The focus areas include healthcare access, agricultural losses, water shortages, mobility, waste management, education, livelihoods, environmental risks and disaster preparedness. national_raw_news.content: Indian Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh and Japan Air Self-Defense Force Chief of Staff General Takehiro Morita flew together in India’s indigenous Light Combat Aircraft Tejas during a formation sortie in Jodhpur today. The flight by the air chiefs of both nations comes as the Indian Air Force and Japan Air Self-Defense Force are conducting the joint air exercise ‘Veer Guardian 2026’ in Jodhpur. This is the first time that Japanese fighter aircraft are operating from Indian soil as part of a bilateral exercise, further deepening the defence partnership between both the countries. Talking to media in Jodhpur after the sortie, Air Chief Marshall Singh said, first-ever operation of Japanese fighter jet on Indian soil marks major milestone in bilateral defence ties. The Japanese Air Chief appreciated the warm hospitality extended by the Indian side and described the Tejas as a symbol of India’s technological innovation and the country’s Make in India initiative The 14-day exercise, which will conclude on Tuesday, focuses on advanced operational missions and extensive professional interactions between the two air forces. The exercise involves a diverse mix of Indian Air Force frontline combat aircraft, including the indigenous Light Combat Aircraft Tejas, Su-30MKI and Rafale while Japan is participating with F-2A fighter aircraft.

national_raw_news.title: 56 mins ago | National 29 President Murmu calls for stronger climate action and global cooperation to tackle rising natural...
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has said numerous natural disasters in recent times have made it clear that robust climate action is essential to mitigate climate impacts. Addressing the valedictory session of the conference on the Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics in New Delhi this evening, the President said the global scientific community is warning that climate risk has become very serious. She stressed on the need to strengthen active cooperation among stakeholders at local, regional, and global levels to prevent and address the issue. The President said, climate change is also having serious repercussions on food security, health, and livelihoods. President Murmu said, it is well known that climate change is causing imbalances across various levels of human existence. She said, biodiversity loss, water stress and land degradation are examples of the imbalances. The President said that farm pods can be useful for the local community in the water-stress regions. She said, a well-structured framework of policies and actions is essential to effectively address such a complex challenge. President Murmu said, the framework must ensure the active participation of not only governments and legal experts but also the communities most affected by climate change. She said, special sensitivity towards the needs of rural and forest-dwelling societies, small farmers, women, and other vulnerable communities is crucial, as they bear the brunt of natural disasters. The President underlined that traditional knowledge systems, along with the practices and lived experiences of local communities, play a vital role in enhancing climate adaptation capacity. She stressed on strengthening climate resilience through people-centric and community-based adaptation approaches rooted in traditional knowledge. President Murmu stated that sustainable afforestation can also play a significant role in enhancing climate resilience. She said, afforestation efforts that nurture biodiversity and are aligned with local conditions can be instrumental in this regard. She added that the true objective of sustainable afforestation is not merely planting trees, but rather restoring healthy and self-sustaining ecosystems. The President said that developing countries should chart a path that enhances resilience while maintaining the pace of development. She said, commitments to responsible climate action must align with the country’s development needs and economic aspirations. She added that they must also be technically feasible. The President said that India has done commendable work in fostering environmental awareness by engaging common citizens, especially the youth. She said, the Government of India’s ‘Mission LiFE’ initiative has demonstrated that meaningful strides towards ecological restoration can be achieved through public participation and community ownership. She said, the National Green Tribunal plays a pivotal role in environment-related legal matters. President Murmu said, the Tribunal has expeditiously resolved a vast number of disputes. She said, the tribunal has developed an effective compliance framework regarding rivers, air quality, and waste management in the country. Union Minister for Power, Housing and Urban Development Manohar Lal, Judge in Supreme Court Justice B V Nagaratna, Chairman National Green Tribunal Justice Prakash Shrivastava, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta also addressed the valedictory session of the conference.

national_raw_news.content: Bogibeel IWT Terminal National Waterway-2 Visit Overview - Pragativadi I Latest Odisha News in English I Breaking News About us Privacy Policy Disclaimer Contact Sunday, September 20, 2026 EPAPER Odisha Twin City Politics National World Sports Entertainment Business Lifestyle Tech Quiz Prativa Vikash 2026 No Result View All Result EPAPER Odisha Twin City Politics National World Sports Entertainment Business Lifestyle Tech Quiz Prativa Vikash 2026 No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home » Bogibeel IWT Terminal and NW-2: How Brahmaputra Waterways Can Transform Northeast and Odisha Logistics Bogibeel IWT Terminal and NW-2: How Brahmaputra Waterways Can Transform Northeast and Odisha Logistics Odisha media team reviews Brahmaputra terminals as IWAI maps a river-to-port logistics model for the Northeast and Odisha by Yajati Rout September 20, 2026 in Odisha Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 0 0 21 VIEWS A media delegation from Odisha, led by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) Bhubaneswar, on Sunday began a five-day exposure tour of Assam to study major infrastructure and logistics projects in the Northeast. The first stop was the Bogibeel Inland Water Transport (IWT) Terminal on the Brahmaputra, along with the 4.94-km Bogibeel Bridge — India’s longest combined rail-and-road span across the river. The visit was designed as more than a site inspection. IWAI officials used the terminal to explain how National Waterway-2 (NW-2) is being built as a low-cost cargo, passenger and strategic corridor — and how a similar model is being prepared for Odisha’s National Waterway-5 (NW-5) on the Brahmani–Mahanadi system. What the terminal can do IWAI official Sunil Shinde briefed the visiting journalists on operations at Bogibeel, commissioned as a modern tourist-cum-cargo facility on NW-2. The terminal has berthing infrastructure for vessels up to 1,000 MT (flotilla) and an annual cargo handling capacity of about 6 lakh metric tonnes. Officials said it currently supports multimodal movement of crude oil and petroleum products from the Dibrugarh belt, besides tea, coal, stone aggregates and cement. The waterway is also being used for heavy Over-Dimensional Cargo (ODC) linked to the capacity expansion of the Numaligarh Refinery. The tourist-cum-cargo terminal received its foundation stone from Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal on 4 July 2023. Construction began around June 2023. In February 2026, Customs and Immigration complexes at Bogibeel and Dhubri were inaugurated, tightening the terminal’s role on the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route. A Regional Centre of Excellence and additional cruise facilities are also being developed at Bogibeel. Why the river route matters NW-2 — the 891-km Brahmaputra stretch from the Bangladesh border to Sadiya — was declared a national waterway on 1 September 1988. About 12 terminals are now maintained for cargo vessels, passenger ferries and Ro-Ro services. Key points include Dhubri, Jogighopa (a Port of Call and multimodal hub), Pandu in Guwahati with rail connectivity, Tezpur, Silghat, Biswanath Ghat, Neamati, Bogibeel, Dibrugarh, Sengajan/Panbari and Oriumghat. IWAI maintains navigable depth through regular dredging: 2.5 metres from the Bangladesh border to Neamati, 2.0 metres from Neamati to Dibrugarh/Bogibeel, and 1.5 metres from Dibrugarh to Sadiya....

national_raw_news.content: Union Sports Minister Mandaviya leads Indian diaspora at 'Sundays on Cycle' in Nagoya to Cheer for Bharat Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Sports Minister Mandaviya leads Indian diaspora at 'Sundays on Cycle' in Nagoya to Cheer for Bharat ANI | Updated: Sep 20, 2026 14:06 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Aichi-Nagoya [Japan], September 20 (ANI): Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Mansukh Mandaviya led the 91st edition of ‘Sundays on Cycle’ at Meijo Park in Nagoya, Japan, on Sunday, September 20, 2026, where he rallied together members of the Indian diaspora to extend support and encouragement to the Indian contingent participating in the Asian Games 2026. The initiative reflected the Government of India's continued efforts to strengthen people-to-people connect with the Indian diaspora through the universal language of sports, while reinforcing the message of fitness and healthy living under the Fit India Movement, as per a press release from the Union Sports Ministry. Mandaviya interacted with participants of the 91st Sundays on Cycle event and appreciated their enthusiasm for coming together to support Team India in the Asian Games. The Indian community in Nagoya came together through ‘Sundays on Cycle’ to ‘Cheer for Bharat’ and boost the morale of the athletes participating on the biggest continental stage. “The Asian Games have commenced in Nagoya, Japan, and we have a contingent of over 500 young athletes from India, who are participating in the Games,” said Dr Mandaviya. “The Indian diaspora in Nagoya has shown great enthusiasm to support and cheer our athletes by joining the Sundays on Cycle event here,” he said. “I am happy to say that our contingent is performing well, and our diaspora is working hard to boost their morale," he added. Mandaviya is in Nagoya, Japan, for the Asian Games 2026, where he is interacting with Indian athletes, officials, and members of the Indian diaspora, underscoring the Government's sustained efforts towards promoting sports excellence and a fitter, healthier India on the global stage. Fit India Sundays on Cycle is organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) in collaboration with the Cycling Federation of India (CFI), Raahgiri Foundation and MY Bharat. The cycling drive is conducted simultaneously across all States and Union Territories, including at SAI Regional Centres, National Centres of Excellence (NCOEs), SAI Training Centres (STCs), Khelo India State Centres of Excellence (KISCEs) and Khelo India Centres (KICs). Over 6000 NAMO Fit India clubs also organise the cycling initiative nationwide every week. national_raw_news.content: Varanasi Gears Up For Three-Day IAF Air Show Over Ganga, PM Modi Likely To Attend States Three-Day IAF Air Show To Be Held In Varanasi In October, PM Modi Likely To Attend Swarajya Staff Sep 20, 2026 | Updated 12:27 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Three IAF Rafales flying in formation. (Via PIB) Varanasi is set to witness its first-ever air show as the Indian Air Force (IAF) prepares to stage a spectacular three-day aerial display over the sacred Ganges. Scheduled for 22, 23 and 25 October, the event is expected to draw crowds of 20 lakh people to witness fighter jets and helicopters performing above the historic ghats stretching from Namo Ghat to Assi Ghat. The Indian Air Force plans to deploy more than three dozen aircraft for the show, including Rafale fighter jets, the renowned Suryakiran aerobatic team, Rudra helicopters, C-295 aircraft, Tejas fighters and Dakota aircraft. Performances will take place between noon and 2pm each day, with displays lasting approximately 90 minutes as three to five aircraft showcase aerial manoeuvres simultaneously over the river. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to attend as chief guest on the final day, with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and senior military officials also likely to participate. Air Force authorities have coordinated extensively with Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport officials, with Suryakiran jets taking off from Varanasi Airport whilst other aircraft will fly from surrounding districts. District administration has begun preparations to manage the anticipated crowds, with special arrangements being made across 84 ghats along the riverfront. Namo Ghat, designated as the main control centre, will be handed over to Air Force control from 16 October, with public access restricted during the setup period. Officials have enlisted support from neighbouring Chandauli, Ghazipur and Jaunpur districts to handle crowd management and security. Rehearsals for the historic event will commence on 20 October and continue through 22 October. The Rajghat bridge and boat services on the Ganges will remain closed during performances for safety reasons. Local authorities are preparing for crowds comparable to the Dev Deepavali festival, with arrangements for approximately 5,000 VIP guests from across India and abroad.
